I've farmed this land my whole life, and my mother farmed it before me. Quzhou is wheat-corn country — that's what the land is suited for, that's what the buyers want, and that's what I know how to do without making mistakes.

My total farmland is about 8 mu. I won't try anything risky this year. I'm 57, my knees hurt in the mornings, and I can't afford a bad harvest. The grain procurement station still buys wheat at a fair price. Corn sells to the feed traders every fall.

For winter wheat, I'll plant in mid-October like always. I'll hire the tractor from the village cooperative for rotary tillage — I stopped doing it by hand years ago. I'll use Jimai 22 seed, same as last few years. It does well here. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then urea at jointing. Three irrigations: before sowing to settle the soil, one in winter to protect roots from freezing, and one at jointing. I spray herbicide in spring and fungicide before heading.

Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed corn — no-tillage, the stubble stays. Hybrid seed from the county supply store. Corn mostly relies on rain here in summer, but if August is dry I'll run the pump once. I top-dress urea at the 10-leaf stage.

I also keep about 1 mu of vegetables near the house — garlic, cabbage, radish, some eggplant. That feeds us and I sell the surplus at the market in Quzhou town on weekends. I rotate through spring and autumn plantings.
